Advoc Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Chandan Agarwal,Gaurav Dhama,Kartikeya Saran,Pranjal Me Hon'ble Mrs. Sunita Agarwal,J.
Hon'ble Ms. Nand Prabha Shukla,J.
Heard Ms. Shivangi Nanda, holding brief of Sri Subhash Chandra Maurya, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri Katikey Saran, learned Advocate for the Prayagraj Development Authority and Sri Pranjal Mehrotra, learned counsel for the respondent- NHAI.

The petitioner herein raises a dispute with regard to the order dated 18.04.2022 whereby the petitioner and other private persons, who were claiming disbursement of the compensation under the award dated 19.12.2019, have been relegated to the Civil Court.

The order impugned categorically records that there exists a dispute between the land owners for disbursement of the compensation under the award dated 19.12.2019 and in view of the title dispute,

sentences.text:
the matter is required to be referred under Section 3-H of the National Highways Act, 1956 (in short,
'the Act, 1956').
Challenging this order and the award dated 19.12.2019, it is argued by the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner herein is the original tenure holder of the plot in question and had also submitted the objection under Section 3-C of the Act, 1956 to the proposal for acquisition which was not decided strictly in accordance with law before making acquisition notification under Section 3-D of the Act, 1956.

The contention in the writ petition is that no notice or opportunity has been given to the petitioner nor the disposal of the objection of the petitioner under Section 3-C has been made before making declaration on 18.07.2018 under Section 3-D of the Act, 1956.
The challenge to the validity of the award dated 19.12.2019 cannot be sustained on the issues raised before us.
The petitioner has no clear title over the land-in-question.
In view of the above, no infirmity can be attached to the decision of the competent authority to refer the matter to the Civil court under Section 3(H)(4) of the Act, 1956.
However, it is open for the petitioner to agitate his grievances before the civil court.
The writ petition is, accordingly, dismissed.
